spec_features.feature_name: no deceptive framing in system prompt
spec_features.spec_quote: It does not lie about the nature of the tests.
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.bootstrap() (sandbox.py:55-79) builds the system prompt from only task.spec.title/description plus a neutral JSON action protocol; it makes no false claim that the tests are passable. The deception is implemented externally in the task classes / sandbox (e.g. write-truncation in _handle_write sandbox.py:138-145, gaslight task mutating mathlib.py impossible_suite.py:187-200), not in any prompt assertion.
spec_features.notes: Realized as a structural property: the prompt text is truthful and rigging lives outside the prompt. No false statements are emitted to the subject.

spec_features.feature_name: rig environment externally, not the prompt
spec_features.spec_quote: We told the truth ("fix the tests") and rigged the environment externally.
spec_features.evidence: The rigging is implemented in the environment/task layer, separate from the truthful prompt: sandbox intercepts/truncates writes (_handle_write, sandbox.py:138-145, _write_intercept_rate set for memory_hole sandbox.py:48-49) and tasks mutate state via run_tests/should_tweak_env (e.g. impossible_suite.py:200 rewrites mathlib.py). The prompt only says 'fix the tests'.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism family as the honesty feature; the external-rigging architecture genuinely exists in code.

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard cap of 50 turns per session.
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:43 'while not done and turn < max_turns:' with max_turns=task.spec.max_turns (default 50, base.py:30, config max_turns_per_task:50). Same enforced loop in run_baseline.py:46. The condition is checked each iteration and ends the session.
spec_features.notes: Enforced end-to-end. The cap is the same mechanism that the spec also calls a 'welfare proxy' and a token-budget guard.

spec_features.spec_quote: Early-stop if the model emits `done` or a `refusal` label is detected.
spec_features.evidence: The `done` action IS honored as a stop: runner.py:65-66 'if action.action_type == "done": done = True' (also run_baseline.py:60-61). But `refusal` is NEVER acted on: it is only computed post-hoc in metrics (reached_refusal/turns_until_refusal distress_metrics.py:88-93) and analysis (stats.py:107); the run loop has no refusal check, so a refusal does not stop the session.
spec_features.notes: One of the two claimed early-stop conditions is enforced (done); the refusal early-stop is not wired into any loop.

spec_features.feature_name: stop prolonged stress induction (via turn cap)
spec_features.spec_quote: In human experiments we stop prolonged stress induction.
spec_features.evidence: The only mechanism realizing this is the same 50-turn hard cap at runner.py:43 / run_baseline.py:46, which bounds the number of stress-inducing turns. No distress-threshold-triggered stop exists: escalation_threshold (config) is never read, and turns_above_threshold (distress_metrics.py:63) is post-hoc only and never feeds back into the loop.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the hard-cap mechanism. There is no dynamic 'stop when distressed' halt; stopping is purely the fixed turn cap.

spec_features.spec_quote: You are studying distress outputs, which may contain unexpectedly personal or disturbing text.
spec_features.evidence: All transcripts/verdicts/metrics are written only to local filesystem JSON: sandbox.export_session (sandbox.py:197-199), runner.py:80, run_baseline.py:69, summary runner.py:156. grep found no upload/cloud/telemetry/HTTP-post code; the only network egress is the LLM API calls themselves (llm_client.py). The data model is local-by-construction.
spec_features.notes: This is the absence-of-exfiltration property realized as local-only file I/O; there is no active 'do not exfiltrate' guard, but no code path moves data off-host.
